content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper describes the use of Energy-Based Models for an application in high-energy physics. The authors propose a permutation-invariant neural network with self-attention for the energy model, which takes in a set of jets. Then it is demonstrated how the generative model can be used to generate events and perform anomaly detection.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- EBMs are applied to an interesting problem with different characteristics than typical image and video data (i.e. sets). 
- The authors have adapted the EBM model to this problem, e.g. by using a permutation-invariant neural network. 

Weaknesses:
- The writing is unclear in many places. The introduction could be more focused on what problem is being addressed, how ideas from ML are being applied in physics, and what this paper has to offer the ML community.
- The results here do not say much about EBMs beyond this application.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The clarity could be improved. This work is an original application of EBMs to physics, and the authors have been thoughtful in how they adapt the methods to the idiosyncrasies of this problem.

Some notes:
- Figure 1 is confusing, and the caption is not helpful.
- Figure 3 caption says left, middle, and right, but there are 5 images. This should be fixed for clarity.
content.summary_of_the_review: While this is certainly an interestnig case study, it is unclear how the results here are general enough to be of much interest to the ICLR community.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors' main contribution is to train Energy-based models (EBMs) for learning jet radiation from High Energy Physics (HEP) events at the Large Hadron Collider. The paper proposes to use EBMs to learn such jets via simulated data using the KL-corrected Contrastive divergence training scheme and perform event generation. They also propose to use EBMs for anomalous event detection directly using the energy scores and a novel hybrid scheme that couples EBMs with a separate neural classifier through a joint-likelihood loss. The HEP event generation results indicate successful learning of the data and generate realistic samples very close to the given p(X). Finally, the anomaly detection results also indicate good classification performance, especially in the case of proposed hybrid modeling.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The authors also successfully demonstrate the effectiveness of EBMs and their ability to reduce spurious signal correlations, which is useful for rare and out-of-distribution (OOD) signal detection. As a result, this framework as a tool has the potential to propel further advancement of the study of Quantum chromodynamics jets and interacting fundamental particles.
Weakness: 
1.	The paper lacks proper baseline comparisons, especially since there exist many relevant works utilizing VAE, GAN, Graph NN architectures, etc., for HEP anomaly detection, jet tagging, and event generation.
2.	In correlation with the above comments, a stronger related work survey would be important to showcase the need for proposing this work.
3.	It is essential to show the false positive, false negative rates and other metrics like precision, recall and learning curves for the anomaly detection experiments.

The authors claim that the following cited papers are unstable to train and would not be able to learn complex input features. However, the below works manage to produce highly accurate generated HEP events and detect anomalies accurately. Looking more closely, some of the works use input features very similar to what the authors utilize to train their EBM. So, it is highly necessary to compare the proposed work with these works for explicit clarity.
-- Kansal, Raghav, et al. "Graph Generative Adversarial Networks for Sparse Data Generation in High Energy Physics." arXiv preprint arXiv:2012.00173 (2020).
-- Butter, Anja, Tilman Plehn, and Ramon Winterhalder. "How to GAN LHC events." SciPost Physics 7.6 (2019): 075.
Touranakou, Mary, et al. "Particle-based Fast Jet Simulation at the LHC with Variational Autoencoders." arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.00520 (2022).
-- Finke, Thorben, et al. "Autoencoders for unsupervised anomaly detection in high energy physics." Journal of High Energy Physics 2021.6 (2021): 1-32.

Moreover, 
-- Zhai, Shuangfei, et al. "Deep structured energy based models for anomaly detection." International conference on machine learning. PMLR, 2016. This paper is another good baseline as it particularly utilizes EBMs trained with score-matching (SM) to perform anomaly detection using naive energy values and gradient norm of energy as decision criteria. The work is relevant in terms of how the proposed paper could perform against another EBM training algorithm such as SM and which also uses energy values directly for anomaly and outlier detection.
-- Kumar, Rithesh, et al. "Maximum entropy generators for energy-based models." arXiv preprint arXiv:1901.08508 (2019). This work is an interesting baseline as it proposes mutual information maximization via Jensen-Shannon divergence instead of KL divergence and claims it is better than KLD loss term in your paper. It would be very interesting to compare the proposed work when JSD is used for training.


Questions:
1.	Out of curiosity, are there any experimental evaluations that include the entropy term in loss computation instead of back-propagating gradients in all Langevin dynamics steps? This is to compare how much of a slowdown in training is happening due to the inclusion of this term and measure any performance difference.
2.	Why is contrastive divergence applied and why not other EBM techniques?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is well-written and clearly presented. It is easy to comprehend and understand.
Applying machine learning algorithms for HEP events has been a well-studied area in recent years, however, utilizing EBMs for HEP is a novel idea.

====
Typos:
1.	Page 5 – sentence error; “we would like to energy function to be powerful enough”.
2.	Page 6 - Inconsistent acronym in the sentence; “there is specificity in EBM-based OoD”.
3.	Page 8 – “THe jointly trained model has even...”.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors have shown the potential of EBMs in learning HEP events and the model’s ability to be versatile in performing various tasks such as event generation and anomaly detection. This can further enable fundamental physics research by generating new anomalous events whose impact can be studied in lieu of actual experimental data. Results showcase a part of the authors' motivation; however, the paper lacks enough evidence that there is a need for an EBM-based HEP learning framework. The paper requires a clarified literature study of all relevant works available and additionally conducts additional baseline experiments to support their claim for proposing EBMs for HEP events.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work advocates for the application of Energy-based Models (EBMs) to High Energy Physics event detection at facilities like the Large Hadron Collider. They show that EBMs can be equivalently used for implicit generation of physics events with a physics-based validation using high-level features such as the transverse momentum and jet mass. In addition, they also show that applying a hybrid learning (with generative and discriminative) EBM have a higher accuracy and OoD detection ability. Major novelty of this work however is the adoption of self-attention-based-transformer to mimic the inter-particle interactions.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

•	The use of EBMs for HEP events is well motivated and the results demonstrate it

•	The transformer network seems to improve the EBMs

•	Physics-based validation is crucial, and results support it


Weaknesses:

•	Not clear what the algorithmic contribution is; the methods provided in section 2 and algorithm1 seem to be already existent. 

•	Recently developed EBM approaches have been effectively applied for HEP event detection but no new machine learning approaches have been proposed


•	Ablation experiments to understand the effect of the effect of various components and especially the transformer network is crucial to understand the model performance

•	How are the hyperparameters for the learning chosen?

•	Do the results hold with multiple random initializations of the model?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written, and algorithmic novelty is low
content.summary_of_the_review: Although application of EBMs to HEP event detection is well motivated, no new ML approaches have been proposed in this work that can be adopted by the general ML community to problems beyond the HEP event detection.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper has proposed a framework to model the behavior of elementary particles with a self-attention transformer for inter-particle interactions and an energy function for correlations in the detector space.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weakness
1. For reviewers without too much physics background, could the author explain what makes the high energy events special at the Large Hadron Collider? What is the difference between the events at Large Hadron Collider and the others? Could the proposed model be used in general high energy events?
2. What is the specific reason to choose self-attention 8(a) to approximate the energy function？
3. For 4.1, there are lots of data visualization methods to show the generation quality. Are there any quantification ways to compare the results? 
4. What would be the results like if replacing the energy function in other ways?

Writing:
1. No need to define the abbreviation for EBM in both abstract and paragraph.
2. The logic in the introduction is disordered, and it looks like the second paragraph is unrelated to the topic in the paper. It is quite hard to see the connection between EBM and HEP events.
3. The author may introduce the topic as this starting from the second paragraph: 1）What are the challenges of HEP events? 2) How did other unsupervised methods solve them? 3) What is the advantage of EBM?
4. Looks like the second paragraph in 4.1 should be moved into the introduction to show the importance of event simulation?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity and Quality: The paper is not very clear. Please refer to point 2 and 3 in the writing suggestions. I don't think the paper is ready for publication considering the current organization in content.

Novelty: I didn’t see new things proposed by the author. The only contribution I find is that the author apply EBM models in a physic environment.
Reproducibility: Looks hard to reproduce if the 50k QCD jets dataset is not available.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper has proposed a framework to model the behavior of elementary particles with a self-attention transformer for inter-particle interactions. However, this paper is hard to read for non-physics readers. Since this is a learning conference,  the author should assume most readers are not familiar with the HEP events in collider experiments. Please refer to my writing suggestions to make clear what is the current challenge and meaning in modeling HEP events and what is the advantage and effects of the proposed modeling method. In summary, I think the paper is not well-written, especially in describing and defining the question for HEP simulation in a physics situation. And many contents in section 1 are unrelated to the topic. Furthermore, simply applying existing methods in a new situation lacks novelty in the method, unless the author could list and compare different modeling strategies.

----Post Rebuttal----
Since the author doesn't respond to my questions. I will keep my original ratings.
